title: Year 7 Summer 1 unit quiz
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 69 (Year 7 Summer 1 unit quiz (portal quiz, secure mode, written for this unit))
intro: Covers lessons 52 to 69 of Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: In square WXYZ (labelled in order), which line segment is a diagonal?
questions.a: B) XZ. X and Z are opposite corners, so XZ is a diagonal. The other three join neighbouring letters, so they are sides.

questions.q: Which angle is reflex?
questions.a: C) 190°. 190° is between 180° and 360°. 175° is obtuse because it is less than 180°.

questions.q: The inside angle is 48°. What is the reflex angle at the same vertex?
questions.a: B) 312°. 360 - 48 = 312. 132° is 180 - 48: that is the angle on a straight line, not round a point.

questions.q: Triangle PQR has PQ = 6 cm and QR = 8 cm. Which angle is the included angle?
questions.a: B) angle Q. Q is the vertex shared by PQ and QR, so angle Q is between them. P and R are at the far ends.

questions.q: Angles of 100° and 90° are given at the two ends of a side. What happens?
options: the arms never meet: no triangle
questions.a: B) the arms never meet: no triangle. 100 + 90 = 190, more than 180°, so the arms move apart. Two angles must add up to less than 180°.

questions.q: Which lengths make a triangle?
questions.a: C) 5 cm, 6 cm, 10 cm. 5 + 6 = 11, more than 10. In the others the two shorter sides add up to less than, or exactly, the longest side.

questions.q: Compasses are set to 3 cm for a 10 cm line. What happens?
questions.a: A) the arcs do not meet. 3 + 3 = 6, less than 10, so the arcs cannot reach each other. Use more than half the line: more than 5 cm.

questions.q: Bisecting a reflex angle of 240° gives:
questions.a: A) 120°. Half of 240 is 120. 60° would come from bisecting the 120° angle on the other side.

questions.q: A point is 4 cm from a line, measured along the perpendicular. A slanted path from the point to the line could be:
questions.a: C) 5 cm. Any other path is longer than the perpendicular, so it must be more than 4 cm. 3 cm is impossible; 4 cm is the perpendicular itself.

questions.q: A hexagon is made by stepping a radius of 5 cm round a circle. Each side is:
questions.a: A) 5 cm. Each side equals the radius, because the six triangles from the centre are equilateral. 10 cm is the diameter.

questions.q: Three equal angles and a right angle meet at a point. Each equal angle is:
questions.a: A) 90°. 360 - 90 = 270, then 270 ÷ 3 = 90. 270 forgets to share between three; 120 ignores the right angle.

questions.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 115°. Which list gives all four?
questions.a: A) 115°, 65°, 115°, 65°. Neighbours add up to 180°: 180 - 115 = 65. 245 wrongly uses 360.

questions.q: Angles x, 2x and 3x lie on a straight line. x =
questions.a: A) 30°. 6x = 180, so x = 30. 60 uses 360 instead of 180.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has one angle of 34°. The third angle is:
questions.a: A) 56°. 180 - 90 - 34 = 56. 146 forgets the right angle.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 120°. Each base angle is:
questions.a: A) 30°. (180 - 120) ÷ 2 = 30. 60 forgets to share between two angles.

questions.q: A kite has angles of 120° and 70°, and its other two angles are the equal pair. Each equal angle is:
questions.a: A) 85°. 360 - 120 - 70 = 170, shared between two equal angles: 85° each. 170 forgets to share.

questions.q: Which symbol means 'is perpendicular to'?
Which type of angle is 135°?
questions.a: B) obtuse

questions.q: The inside angle is 100°. The reflex angle is:
Which set of facts fixes exactly one triangle?
questions.a: B) two sides and the angle between them
options: two sides and the angle between them
